descriptions.text: Self transfer in _transfer() Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xbeefd8faba2aa82704afe821fd41b670319203dd9090f7af8affdf6bcfec2d61 Analysis: https://twitter.com/ImmuneBytes/status/1664239580210495489

The DeezNutz ERC-404 implementation contained an accounting error in self-transfers. ERC-404 is a hybrid ERC-20/ERC-721 token that mints or burns NFT units whenever an address's balance crosses a whole-token threshold; in a self-transfer the same address is both sender and receiver. The contract credited the receiver balance without properly debiting the sender (or triggered an NFT mint for the receive leg without a corresponding burn for the send leg), effectively inflating the caller's balance on each self-transfer. The attacker flash-loaned 2,000 WETH, swapped into DeezNutz, performed five self-transfer iterations to multiply holdings, transferred a small portion to the pair to satisfy the Uniswap k-value check, then swapped the inflated balance back to WETH for profit. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: 0xbeefd8faba2aa82704afe821fd41b670319203dd9090f7af8affdf6bcfec2d61 Analysis: DeezNutz 404 Exploit

DeezNutz_404 was exploited on Ethereum on 2024-02-21 after an ERC-404 token implementation mishandled self transfers. The attacker repeatedly transferred DN tokens to the same address, inflated the balance through faulty accounting, then sold the unbacked tokens for about 58.65 ETH. The DeezNutz_404 ERC-404 token implementation failed to handle transfer() calls where the sender and recipient were the same address. Cached balance values were updated in the wrong order, so a self transfer increased the attacker's balance instead of leaving it unchanged. The attacker repeatedly self transferred tokens to mint unbacked supply and drained liquidity from the DN/WETH market.

I might otherwise skip over news of a $170,000 hack, given how commonly thefts of that scale happen in the crypto world, but with a name like this... come on. One thing that keeps me from ever trying my hand as a crypto project hacker is that if I made $170,000 from exploiting a project called "DeezNutz_404", I would immediately be caught because I wouldn't be able to resist telling everyone I know that I'd just made enough money to not have to work for a couple years by exploiting deez nuts . Anyway, there was a bug in their code that allowed an attacker to mint infinite tokens and steal around 58.65 ETH (~$170,000).
